GOAL prove `putnam_2008_b5` in full, both directions.

FACT the reverse direction is routine: `x + n` and `-x + n` are `ContDiff`, and `den (±q + n) = den q`.

FACT the forward direction requires showing every C^1 `f` with the denominator property is `±x + n`.

HYP that forward direction needs a non-trivial analytic-arithmetic argument (Lipschitz bounds on the reduced-fraction lattice, plus a density or Baire-type step to pin the derivative to ±1 globally).

CHECK whether I have a complete, formalizable argument for the forward direction.

RESULT I do not have one. Every route I considered either fails to force `f' = ±1` or leaves a gap that would need substantial Lean infrastructure that is not available here (no Mathlib sources, no network). I did not write or compile any partial proof, so `/work/putnam_2008_b5.lean` is unchanged.

I give up.
